COMPANY DESCRIPTION: Alibaba is China's version of Amazon, Google Cloud, PayPal, and eBay all rolled into one. It is the biggest e-commerce company in the world by gross merchandise volume (GMV) and operates online shopping platforms including Tmall, Taobao, Alibaba.com, AliExpress, and Lazada. Beyond shopping, it runs a cloud computing business, a logistics network, digital media, and is pushing into A.I. Headquartered in Hangzhou, China. Founded in 1999 by Jack Ma. Alibaba doesn’t make things, it runs platforms that connect buyers and sellers and takes fees, ads, and services revenue.
Four Segments:

1. China E-commerce (~52% of rev): The heart of the company. Includes Taobao, Tmall, the B2B platform 1688, and food delivery service Ele.me. Forecast to generate around CN¥565 billion in 2026. Taobao is like a giant online flea market where anyone can sell. Tmall is like a premium digital mall for established brands. Makes money through seller advertising, transaction fees, merchant services

2. International Digital Commerce (~13 of rev): Replicating the China marketplace globally. Includes AliExpress and Lazada (Southeast Asia), Trendyol (Turkey), Daraz (South Asia), with a strategic focus on key regions including select European markets and the Gulf Region. Growing fast but still small.

RECOMMENDATION: AstraZeneca is a world-class, large-cap, profitable business that is still in a high-growth phase, with a pipeline that provides visibility well into the 2030s.

COMPANY DESCRIPTION: One of the world's largest pharma companies, headquartered in Cambridge, UK focused on several major disease areas: cancer (oncology is the largest (~40% of rev), heart and kidney disease, respiratory conditions like asthma and COPD, and rare diseases. Key products: cancer drug Tagrisso ($7.3bn 2025 rev), cholesterol drug Farxiga ($8.4bn), COVID-19 vaccine developed with Oxford University. Stated goal to deliver $80bn in total rev by 2030 (vs $58.7bn in 2025) via growth in its existing oncology, biopharma, and rare disease portfolio, and by launching 20 new medicines.

Oncology (~40% of rev): Largest, fastest-growing segment. Generated $24bn in 2025, +17% y-o-y. Key drugs include Tagrisso (lung cancer), Imfinzi (lung, liver, biliary cancers), Enhertu (HER2 cancers, ADC), Lynparza (ovarian, breast, prostate), and Calquence (blood cancers).

Cardio, Renal & Metabolism (~22% of rev): Key drugs include Farxiga/Forxiga (heart failure, kidney disease, diabetes), Brilinta (heart attack prevention — now in decline due to generics), Lokelma (potassium management), and Roxadustat.

Respiratory & Immunology (~15% of rev): Key drugs include Fasenra (severe asthma), Breztri (COPD), Saphnelo (lupus), and Airsupra (asthma rescue inhaler). Tozorakimab — currently in late-stage trials for COPD — is the major pipeline bet here.

headings: BP plc [BP/ LN; BP US] Research Note
first: BP plc [BP/ LN; BP US] Research Note
RECOMMENDATION: Maintain position in IDVZ

COMPANY DESCRIPTION: BP is one of the world’s largest oil and gas companies, founded in 1908 as the Anglo-Persian Oil Company. BP finds oil and gas, extracts it, ships it around the world, refines it into fuel, and sells it to consumers and businesses. BP has operations in 61 countries, produced ~2.4 mm barrels per day of oil equivalent, and had total proven reserves of over 6bn barrels. BP also runs around 21,200 service stations worldwide under the BP, Amoco (US), and Aral (Germany) brands. 2025 replacement ratio increased to 90% from 50%. BP earns through three interlocking mechanisms. 1) sells crude oil and nat gas at market prices (highly sensitive to the Brent crude oil price and European/US natural gas benchmarks). 2) earns a refining margin — the spread between what it pays for crude and what it receives for refined products like petrol, diesel, and jet fuel. 3) earns retail and services income from Castrol lubricants, aviation fueling, and convenience stores.

Geographical breakdown: BP's upstream production is split roughly 40% US, 25% Middle East, 15% North Sea (UK/Europe), and 20% Asia-Pacific. The US is the single largest geography through BPX Energy (shale) and Gulf of America operations. BP has committed to growing US production to approximately 1mm boe/d by decade's end.

Dividend: Div cut 50% in 2020 during COVID, a significant trust-breaking event for income investors. The dividend has been rebuilt since but has not returned to pre-2020 levels. Buyback: BP suspended buybacks in 2025 to focus on debt reduction. It will resume once net debt hits the $14–18 bn target range

headings: Canadian National Railway [CNR CN] Research Note
first: Canadian National Railway [CNR CN] Research Note
RECOMMENDATION: Initiate ~2% position in IDVZ

COMPANY DESCRIPTION: Largest freight railway in Canada and the only North American railroad that touches all three coasts (Atlantic at Halifax, Pacific at Vancouver/Prince Rupert, and the Gulf of Mexico at New Orleans). Founded in 1919 by the Canadian gov & privatized in 1995 (largest privatization in Canadian history at the time) CNR is the backbone of the Canadian economy, transporting goods valued at approximately C$250 bn annually. CNR moves grain from Saskatchewan prairies to export terminals, oil from Alberta to refineries, intermodal shipping containers between ports and factories, potash to Asia, lumber to the U.S., chemicals between industrial hubs. The network spans approximately 20K route miles connecting businesses across 8 Canadian provinces and 16 U.S. states. It is the circulatory system of the Canadian economy.

Revenue is a function of 3 variables: volume (carloads or containers), yield/price (freight rate per unit), and fuel surcharges. Also earns ancillary rev from logistics services (trucking, transloading, warehousing, customs brokerage). Freight revenues are derived from 7 commodity groups representing a diversified and balanced portfolio of products.

In 2025, CN generated ~C$17.7 bn in rev: grain and fertilizers (~23%), petroleum and chemicals (~21%), intermodal containers (~22%), metals & minerals (~11%), forest products (~10%), automotive (~5%), & coal (~5%). 35% of rev relate to overseas traffic, 32% to transborder traffic (Canada–U.S. cross-border), 17% to Canadian domestic traffic, and 16% to U.S. domestic traffic. In Q4 2025 CN's operating ratio improved to 61.2%, and for the full year 2025 it came in at 61.9%. The long-term aspiration is to break below 60%, which would put CN among the most efficient Class I railroads in North America. Overseas and transborder together constitute 2/3rds of rev, making it sensitive to international trade flows, FX, and geopolitics.

first: COPA [CPA US] Research Note

RECOMMENDATION: 1-2% position in IDVZ Copa owns the only viable connecting point for thin intra-Americas air routes. Low-cost structure produces 20%+ op margins. Strong balance sheet (0.7x net debt/EBITDA), 13% structural tax rate, & a contracted fleet plan delivering 8–12% annual capacity growth through 2028. Trading at 8-9x earnings with a ~5% dividend yield.

COMPANY DESCRIPTION: Panama's flag carrier providing airline passenger and cargo service flying international routes from its Panama City hub, and domestic Colombian service and international flights from Colombian cities. Copa Colombia also operates Wingo, a low-cost brand. Panama sits at the geographic waist of the Americas, and Copa uses Tocumen International Airport as a connecting funnel (the "Hub of the Americas") linking dozens of secondary cities in North, Central, and South America and the Caribbean that lack the traffic to support direct flights to each other. A passenger flying Guayaquil–Montreal or Córdoba–Havana connects through Panama City. The airline serves 87 destinations in 32 countries, most of which couldn't be economically linked any other way. It's essentially a toll-road on intra-Americas connectivity, run with a single fleet family (Boeing 737NG/MAX) for cost discipline. Revenue is 95% passenger tickets

Capacity (ASM) growth via fleet expansion is the primary lever with 11–13% capacity growth guided for 2026, filled at high load factors (May 2026 system load factor of 88.2%, with RPMs up 17% YoY). Secondary drivers: new spoke cities (the model works at remarkably thin frequencies), Venezuela restoration, underlying Latin American middle-class travel penetration (still far below developed-market trips per capita), Wingo capturing price-sensitive point-to-point demand, & cargo. Rev growth of 17% is projected for FY2026.
INVESTMENT THESIS:

Structural cost advantage + full-service revenue: Copa runs the lowest unit costs among full-service LatAm carriers (single fleet type, low-cost Panama labor base, dense hub) while earning network-carrier yields — the source of industry-leading profitability, with a 24.6% operating margin and 20.2% net margin in Q1 2026, margins that U.S. legacy carriers can only dream about.
RECOMMEDATION: Consider adding 50-100bps in IDVZ taking it to 150-200bps

Operationally strong quarter with results predictably impacted by fuel costs, which will come down as the war in Iran subsides and oil prices comes down sustainably. My focus is on available seat mile and growth at high load levels, which drives revenue and earnings assuming consistent fuel costs.

While the operating margin of 8.7% was a notable decline from the 21.7% recorded in the same period last year, management highlighted the airline's ability to recover approximately 40% of the year-over-year fuel expense increase through higher yields.

2026 guidance is for operating margins of 17-19% and ASM growth of 14-15%. Guidance assumes a load factor of ~87%, unit revenues (RASM) of 12.0 cents, unit costs excluding fuel (Ex-Fuel CASM) of ~5.7 cents, and an all-in fuel price of US$3.60 per gallon.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte (OMA) reported solid Q2 2026 results, characterized by resilient margins and strong non-aeronautical revenue growth that offset a slight miss in aeronautical income. While it is a challenging operating environment for Mexican airports, OMA still delivered positive growth across traffic, revenue, and EBITDA during the period. It was the only major operator in the sector to do this.

OMA reported a beat on both the top and bottom lines relative to the average analyst projections. Total revenue reached MXN 3,622 mm, which was 2.5% higher than the consensus estimate of MXN 3,532 mm.

Investment thesis: OMA operates 13 airports in northern and central Mexico under a concession running to 2048, anchored by Monterrey (~half of traffic), Mexico's industrial capital. It is the purest listed play on nearshoring: its catchment covers the manufacturing corridor (Nuevo León, Chihuahua, Tamaulipas) where US-bound supply-chain relocation drives business travel, cargo, and industrial real estate demand. OMA uniquely monetizes the latter through its industrial park and OMA Carga logistics businesses, diversifying beyond passenger fees. The regulated dual-till model provides inflation-linked tariff visibility via five-year Master Development Programs, while unregulated commercial revenue (still underpenetrated versus ASUR/GAP) offers a self-help margin lever. The business converts EBITDA to cash at industry-leading margins (~75%+), carries modest leverage, and returns essentially all free cash flow through dividends and buybacks.

OMA's financial performance was bolstered by disciplined cost control and successful commercial initiatives.

The company describes itself as a supply chain-based technology and service provider operating in China and Europe. Its reputation in China rests on product authenticity (no counterfeits) and very fast delivery, often same-day or next-day. 80–85% of revenue is product sales (retail: JD buys goods and resells them, low-margin, high-volume), with the balance from services (marketplace commissions and advertising from third-party merchants, plus logistics services sold to external customers). RECOMMENDATION: Maintain Position in IDVZ

COMPANY DESCRIPTION: French energy giant & one of the world's seven "supermajor" oil companies. Total finds oil and gas in the ground, pumps it out, ships it, refines it into gasoline and chemicals, sells it at gas stations, and increasingly generates and sells electricity from renewables and natural gas. Has customers in ~130 countries. Founded in 1924, and rebranded from "Total" to "TotalEnergies" in 2021 to signal a pivot toward being a broader energy company. 100,000+ employees as of 2025.

Exploration & Production (E&P): The core engine. Finds and extracts oil and gas. Produced ~2.5mm barrels of oil equivalent per day (boe/d) in 2025. Generated $15bn in operating income and $15bn in cash flow in 2025. Operating costs are notably low at under $5/boe, making it competitive even in lower-price environments.

Integrated LNG: Covers the entire LNG chain, production, liquefaction, shipping, and global trading. Sold 44mm tons of LNG in 2025. $4.9bn in adjusted net operating income and $5bn in Cash flow. TotalEnergies is one of the world's largest LNG players, with a 50% production growth target in this segment from 2024–2030.

Integrated Power: The "new" business: electricity generation from renewables (solar, wind, hydro) and flexible gas-fired plants. Net electricity generation grew ~17% year-over-year to 48 TWh in 2025. Gross renewable installed capacity reached 34 GW by end of 2025, targeting 100+ TWh of annual net production by 2030. $2bn of cash flow in 2025.
